title: Left-Quillen transport of special cosimplicial frames
statement: Use the model-category axioms and Reedy structures of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $T:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$ be an adjunction whose left functor preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Let $X$ be cofibrant. Let $S:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ be Reedy cofibrant with $S^0=X$ and augmentation $p:S\to\operatorname{const}X$ that is objectwise a weak equivalence with $p^0=1_X$. Let $S':\Delta\to\mathcal N$ be Reedy cofibrant with $S'^0=TX$ and augmentation $p':S'\to\operatorname{const}(TX)$ that is a Reedy trivial fibration with $p'^0=1_{TX}$. Then $TS$ is Reedy cofibrant and there exists a natural transformation $a:TS\to S'$ with $p'a=T(p)$ and $a^0=1_{TX}$, all of whose components are weak equivalences. Moreover $T$ sends every weak equivalence between cofibrant objects to a weak equivalence; in particular all structure and augmentation maps of $TS$ are weak equivalences.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Theorem 5.2.8 (printed p.128), Proposition 5.4.7 (p.132), Lemma 5.5.1 (p.133); agent extraction of the Reedy lifting and comparison argument in the parent former step 12.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to $T\dashv U$ and to each latching diagram of $S$. These diagrams are small: their objects are nonidentity injections into a fixed finite ordinal and their arrows are commuting triangles. The canonical isomorphism $L_n(TS)\cong T(L_nS)$ identifies the latching map into $T(S^n)$ with $T(L_nS\to S^n)$, because both agree on every latching coprojection. The latter is a cofibration by the hypothesis on $T$ and the Reedy cofibrancy of $S$. Cofibrations are unchanged by these isomorphisms: transport any lifting square across the isomorphism and use their left-lifting characterization in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Thus $TS$ is Reedy cofibrant. This includes $n=0$, whose latching category is empty; the same colimit-preservation statement identifies $T0$ with an initial object, so $TX$ is cofibrant.

source.place: Stacks 0038 (categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1); Hovey Theorem 5.2.5, latching characterization; transport of latching maps written out.

proof.text: Let $f:A\to B$ be any weak equivalence between cofibrant objects of $\mathcal M$. The cofibrant clause of [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] gives $i:A\to V$ and $s:B\to V$ cofibrations and $q:V\to B$ a trivial fibration, with $qi=f$ and $qs=1_B$. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] makes $i$ and $s$ weak equivalences, hence trivial cofibrations. Therefore $T(i)$ and $T(s)$ are weak equivalences by assumption. Since $T(q)T(s)=1_{TB}$, two-out-of-three makes $T(q)$ a weak equivalence, and then $T(f)=T(q)T(i)$ is one too. This proves the moreover clause without presuming that $T$ preserves trivial fibrations.

source.place: Hovey Lemma 1.1.12, printed pp. 6-7; split factorization supplied by the existing Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The objectwise-cofibrancy conclusion of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] applies to $S$, so every $S^n$ is cofibrant; $X$ is cofibrant by hypothesis. Step 2 therefore sends every augmentation component $p^n:S^n\to X$ to a weak equivalence. For any $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, naturality gives $p^n S(\theta)=p^m$; since both augmentation components are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three makes $S(\theta)$ one too. Its two endpoints are cofibrant, so step 2 makes $T(S(\theta))$ a weak equivalence. This proves every claimed structure-map and augmentation-map assertion for $TS$.

source.place: Hovey Lemma 1.1.12 and Definition 5.2.7; the augmentation naturality equation and two-out-of-three.

proof.text: Write $0_\Delta$ for the constant diagram at the initial object of $\mathcal N$, which is initial in its cosimplicial diagram category. In the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], form the commutative square with upper map $0_\Delta\to S'$, left map $0_\Delta\to TS$, right map $p':S'\to\operatorname{const}(TX)$, and lower map $T(p)$. It commutes by initiality. Step 1 makes its left map a Reedy cofibration, while its right map is a Reedy trivial fibration by hypothesis. The lifting axiom gives a natural transformation $a:TS\to S'$ with $p'a=T(p)$. In degree zero this equation is $1_{TX}a^0=T(1_X)=1_{TX}$, hence $a^0=1_{TX}$. Reedy weak equivalences are objectwise, so each $p'^n$ is a weak equivalence. Step 3 gives the same property for $T(p^n)$; the equation $p'^n a^n=T(p^n)$ and two-out-of-three prove that every $a^n$ is a weak equivalence.

The transported latching map equals T(L_nS->S^n) because the two agree on coprojections. That map is a cofibration, and cofibrations are closed under isomorphism by their LLP characterization. For n=0, T0 is initial, so TX is cofibrant. Step 2: Ken Brown from the split factorization (qi=f, qs=1). Step 3: Reedy cofibrant implies objectwise cofibrant, so step 2 applies to every p^n and, by naturality and two-out-of-three, to every S(theta). Step 4: lift 0_Delta->TS (a Reedy cofibration by step 1) against p' (a Reedy trivial fibration by hypothesis). p'^0=1 and T(p^0)=1 force a^0=1, and objectwise weak equivalences plus two-out-of-three give every a^n. Small cases checked: identity adjunction, n=0, X not fibrant. No new nodes. No duplicate found by rg; the simplicial-frame-comparison node is the dual statement.
